## Summary

Track the cleanup of open issues older than 30 days whose requested outcome is already implemented, superseded by a stronger current mechanism, obsolete after the TypeScript cutover, redundant with pre-existing work, or deliberately rejected.

This is a short-lived disposal batch under [#886](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/886), not a new product epic. Filing this tracker does **not** itself authorize the closures.

**Canonical current shape: [pass-2](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3915#issuecomment-5466380241).** This body is the pass-1 plan reconciled to that comment on 2026-08-30. Where the two disagree, the current-shape comment wins.

A pass-2 design-critique arc re-derived this audit's evidence against the tree at c6761881 instead of trusting its citations, and changed six of the twenty-five dispositions. Of the 25 candidates: **19 close as filed, 3 must not close on the pass-1 rationale, and 3 close only after sequencing or corrected evidence.** The arc also found the keep-open list wrong about three of its own members. Arc record: [critic](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3915#issuecomment-5466079938), [accepted lean](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3915#issuecomment-5466088929), [verified-claims table](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3915#issuecomment-5466135488), [synthesis](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3915#issuecomment-5466136892).

## Audit boundary

- Repository: deftai/directive
- Evaluated population: 456 open issues older than 30 days
- Filing-time cutoff: 2026-07-30T03:21:43Z
- Canonical upstream revalidation: [c6761881](https://github.com/deftai/directive/commit/c6761881914d3eb02f44f379f9e1e02a94ff708f)
- Pass-1 method: deterministic issue-eval over the full population, followed by REST body/comment reads and implementation/PR verification for closure candidates
- Pass-1 result: 13 implemented or replaced by stronger mechanisms; 12 obsolete, redundant, superseded, or rejected
- Pass-2 method: design-critique refutation arc, N=1, cross-family critic, anchors re-derived against the tree and REST rather than read from the pass-1 citations
- Pass-2 result: 19 dispositions survive; 3 rest on premises that are false at c6761881; 3 need sequencing or corrected evidence; 3 members of the keep-open list are already closed; the exception-set completeness claim is unsupported
- Pass-2 coverage limits: #973, #1283, #1422, and #2518 were verified by sampling only. Keep-open entries #642, #830, #949, #1084, #1883, and #2784 were examined by neither pass.

## Completion criteria

- [ ] The 19 surviving candidates are closed with an evidence comment that cites re-derived evidence, not the pass-1 rationale alone.
- [ ] #973, #1283, #1422, and #2518 receive full verification before their closure comments are written.
- [ ] #513, #602, and #630 are re-disposed — re-scoped, re-anchored, or re-targeted — and are not closed on the pass-1 rationale.
- [ ] #1994 is closed before the #1993 umbrella is refreshed and closed.
- [ ] #2769's canonical current-shape comment is named and refreshed, and its stale "not yet shipped" line retracted, before closure.
- [ ] Every candidate carrying proposed, pending, or active xBRIEF state is lifecycle-reconciled before closure. That set is #630 and #760; re-derive it rather than assuming this list is closed.
- [ ] The corrected keep-open list remains open, and its six unexamined entries are verified before the list is relied on.
- [ ] The canonical current-shape comment records the final counts and is edited in place to pass-3, then this tracker is closed.

## A. Close as filed (19)

Pass-1 rationale re-derived against the tree at c6761881.

## B. Must not close on the pass-1 rationale (3)

Each of these was listed as disposable on a premise that is false at c6761881. Re-dispose them; do not write a closure comment citing the pass-1 reason.

- [ ] [#513](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/513) — the pass-1 reason ("verify:stubs is blocking through task check:merge") does not hold. Branch protection on master requires exactly one check, `TypeScript (build + lint + test)`; the merge-gate job that carries verify:stubs is explicitly not required. The scanner also reads only `.py` / `.go` / `.sh`, so TypeScript stubs are never scanned, and AC3 (README/CONTRIBUTING naming the local equivalent) is unmet. Re-scope it, or close it as deliberately descoped and say so.
- [ ] [#602](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/602) — the cited [#13](https://github.com/deftai/directive/pull/13) is a release-sync merge from 2026-03-09, six weeks before #602 was filed, and no latent-versus-deterministic principle exists in `content/`. Keep it open, or close it against a real anchor.
- [ ] [#630](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/630) — the migrator was renamed, not removed: `tasks/migrate.yml` is live and the verb is `migrate:xbrief`. The requested render-task auto-invocation is still unimplemented, so close it on value if at all — not on non-existence — and re-target its proposed xBRIEF rather than cancelling it on a false premise.

## C. Close only after sequencing or corrected evidence (3)

- [ ] [#760](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/760) — substantively delivered; Actions are on current majors through [#1221](https://github.com/deftai/directive/pull/1221) and [#1222](https://github.com/deftai/directive/pull/1222). But it carries its own proposed brief (`xbrief/proposed/2026-04-23-roadmap-11-upgrade-github-actions-to-node-js-24.xbrief.json`), so it belongs in the reconciliation wave, not the leaf sweep. `verify:orphan-active` fails closed on active briefs only, so nothing machine-catches a proposed one.
- [ ] [#1598](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/1598) — closable, but [#3478](https://github.com/deftai/directive/pull/3478) is the delivery-proof half, which the issue's own last comment separates from its retained scope. The closure comment must cite the handoff-evidence surface (build-skill work/ship/gate axes and `validateHandoffEvidence`) and answer that comment.
- [ ] [#2769](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/2769) — both children and the post-compact rebind shipped in [#3172](https://github.com/deftai/directive/pull/3172). It carries two maintainer current-shape comments ([pass-2](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/2769#issuecomment-5208797067), [pass-3](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/2769#issuecomment-5208865066)), so name one canonical, say what happens to the other, and have the refresh retract the "contract freeze — product not yet shipped" line rather than append under it.

## Required execution order

1. Repair this artifact before any closure: the corrections in this body and the pass-2 current shape.
2. Complete full verification for #973, #1283, #1422, and #2518.
3. Close the 19 in section A, #1994 before #1993, each with an evidence comment.
4. Re-dispose #513, #602, #630; reconcile #760's proposed xBRIEF; close #1598 and #2769 on corrected evidence.
5. Verify final counts, edit the canonical current-shape comment in place to pass-3, and close this tracker.

- [#2784](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/2784) — public promotion remains explicitly deferred. *Not examined by either pass.*

The stated reason applies only to the CRUD chain enumerated above.

## F1. #513's rationale fails on both legs: the gate is not blocking, and it does not scan the product language

`blocks-the-design`

**Evidence.** `gh api repos/deftai/directive/branches/master/protection` returns exactly one required check: `TypeScript (build + lint + test)`. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` lines 52-63 say so in the job map itself: "Live branch protection requires ONLY the TypeScript aggregator. Go and merge-gate aggregators are not required." `verify:stubs` reaches CI only through the `merge-gate` job (`ci.yml:181-182`, `task check:merge` -> `Taskfile.yml:411-423` `check:framework-source` -> `verify:stubs`) -- the job that is explicitly not required. Separately, `packages/core/src/verify-source/verify-stubs.ts:12` pins `EXTENSIONS = new Set([".py", ".go", ".sh"])` and `EXCLUDE_DIRS` adds `scripts`. There are 0 `scripts/*.py` files, no `pyproject.toml`, no `uv.lock`. CHANGELOG (#3481 entry) calls it "a gate that reads only `.py` / `.go` / `.sh`". #513 AC3 ("README.md or CONTRIBUTING.md mentions `task verify:stubs` as the local equivalent") is also unmet -- no match in either file.

**Failure mode.** A PR introducing `TODO` / `FIXME` / `return null` in `.ts` product source merges with no signal at all, and even a merge-gate failure does not block the merge because that check is not required.

**Disposition consequence.** #513 must not close as implemented. Either re-scope it (extend `EXTENSIONS` to `.ts` and make merge-gate required, or fold the scan into the required TS lane) or close it as deliberately descoped and say so. The one-line rationale asserts "blocking" and the tree does not support it.

## F2. #602's cited anchor does not exist, and the requested artifact is absent from the tree

**Evidence.** The rationale cites PR #13. `gh api repos/deftai/directive/pulls/13` is "merge: sync master with beta (v0.5.2)", merged 2026-03-09 -- six weeks *before* #602 was filed (2026-04-23), and a release sync merge is not a principle. Grep for `latent` across `content/` returns only #480 trap-taxonomy hits (`meta/security.md`, `vbrief/vbrief.md`, `conventions/references.md`, `patterns/agent-skill-supply-chain.md`); none is a latent-vs-deterministic coding principle. `content/coding/coding.md` has no such heading. #602's body pre-empts this exact rationale: "Directive's `coding/coding.md` has 'use task for repeatable operations' but never frames this as a first-class architectural principle with a hard rule."

**Failure mode.** The closure records a shipped principle that no file carries. The next agent looking for the named rule finds nothing, and the closure comment is the misleading evidence it finds instead.

**Disposition consequence.** #602 fails the batch. Keep it open, or close it as rejected/duplicate against a real anchor (the Rule Authority [AXIOM] / determinism-tier material) -- not PR #13.
